description:
Dogs can see color — but not the full rainbow. Their world is blue, yellow and gray: reds and greens look like grayish shades to them.
Scientists found dogs have only two color receptors (humans have three), so their vision is like a red-green colorblind person's — and lab tests show dogs actually use color to tell objects apart.
New animal-behaviour facts from the OTIS channel — short, punchy, real science.
